The URD states that, to the Company's knowledge, no other shareholder held 5% or more.

notes: All figures from the LVMH 2025 Universal Registration Document (fiscal year ended December 31, 2025), the PDF hosted on LVMH's own content CDN (lvmh-com.cdn.prismic.io, linked from lvmh.com/en/investors). EUR, converted exactly from EUR millions. OWNERSHIP: Bernard Arnault personally holds 946,055 shares ('in a personal capacity', Board membership as of December 31, 2025); the URD gives no percentage, so pctEconomic is null (for reference only, about 0.19% of the 497,686,940 shares; not disclosed). The relevant holding is the Arnault family group's 49.77% of share capital (65.89% of votes exercisable at Shareholders' Meetings; 65.77% of theoretical votes), recorded in family. That figure includes Christian Dior SE's 42.17%, so Christian Dior SE is not listed separately. Whether Bernard Arnault's personal shares are inside the family-group total is not stated; they are not added. Relation is 'chair' (Chairman and CEO since 1989; reappointed by the Board on April 17, 2025). CDC: the URD gives the CDC Group's 1.24% (and CDC's direct 1%) as of its last threshold crossing on April 16, 2025, not December 31; the group figure is used and the direct 1% is not added to it. Percentages of share capital include the 1,295,928 treasury shares (0.26%) in the denominator. About 900,000 shareholders in total (Euroclear survey, December 2025). BUYBACKS: EUR 1,320.8m paid for 2,550,539 shares bought to be retired (parent-company note 13.1), the same rule as last year: purchases covering bonus share plans (579,981 shares, EUR 320.4m) and the liquidity contract (394,947 shares, round-trip) are not counted as cash returned to shareholders. This ties to §4.1.1 (517,973 shares at an average EUR 585.62 plus 2,032,566 at EUR 500.58, all for 'shares pending retirement'). It includes the EUR 1 billion programme of February–November 2025 (1,899,397 shares; note 16.3) plus 651,142 further shares bought for retirement. For reference: gross purchases of all kinds were 3,525,467 shares, EUR 1,863m (cash impact EUR 1,862m, note 16.3), and the cash-flow statement shows a net 'Acquisition and disposal of LVMH shares' of EUR (1,640)m inside 'Other equity-related transactions'. 2,654,760 shares were retired in 2025. DIVIDENDS: EUR 6,465m paid by LVMH SE; the cash-flow line of EUR (7,123)m also includes EUR 414m paid to minority interests and EUR 244m of tax on intra-group dividends, both excluded. STOCK COMP: Note 17.4 expense of EUR 165m, all bonus share plans (no LVMH Shares expense in 2025). PLAN: the URD describes the 2024 LVMH Shares offer and says employees held the equivalent of less than 1% of the share capital at December 31, 2025, in employee savings plans and as registered bonus shares.
